neuronio-artificial.d: The basic unit of a neural network: it computes \( z = \mathbf w^\top \mathbf x + b \) (a weighted sum of the inputs plus a bias) and returns \( f(z) \), where \( f \) is the activation function. In an LLM, each row of a weight matrix is a neuron.

vies.d: Constant term \( b \) added to a neuron's weighted sum. It shifts the decision boundary without rotating it. The decoders of the recipe LLMs skip the bias in their projections (attention_bias: false); the vision towers still use it (Qwen's and GLM's ViTs, DeepSeek's Aligner).

pre-ativacao.d: The value \( z = \mathbf w^\top \mathbf x + b \) of a neuron before the activation function. In gated layers, the pre-activation of the gate branch is what goes through the sigmoid or the SiLU.

funcao-de-ativacao.d: A nonlinear function applied elementwise after a linear layer (ReLU, GELU, SiLU, sigmoid…). Without it, stacking linear layers would be equivalent to a single linear layer.

camada-linear.d: The transformation \( \mathbf y = W\mathbf x + \mathbf b \) with \( W \in \mathbb R^{m\times n} \): \( m \) neurons side by side, one per row. Checkpoints store \( W \) with shape [out, in]; it costs \( 2mn \) FLOPs per token.

saturacao-ativacao.d: A region where an activation's curve is almost flat (sigmoid and tanh for large |z|). There the derivative is nearly zero and the gradient barely gets through. Not to be confused with saturation by clamp before converting to FP8 (chapter 4).

sigmoide.d: \( \sigma(z) = 1/(1+e^{-z}) \), which maps any number into (0, 1). Saturating as a hidden activation, it is the standard function for gates: the GDN, attention, Gated Residual and PLE gates (Qwen), router, KDA and mHC (GLM), mHC and hc_head (DeepSeek).

tanh.d: Hyperbolic tangent, \( \tanh(z) = 2\sigma(2z)-1 \), with output in (−1, 1) and centered at zero. Today it appears inside the approximate GELU and the logit softcap \( c\cdot\tanh(z/c) \).

relu.d: \( \max(0, z) \): the cheapest activation, with derivative 0 or 1. In the recipes, it scores the sparse attention indexers: \( \sum_h w_h\,\mathrm{ReLU}(\mathbf q_h\cdot\mathbf k) \) in GLM's DSA and DeepSeek's lightning indexer; \( \sum_h \mathrm{ReLU}(\mathbf q_h\cdot\bar{\mathbf k}_b) \), with no per-head weight and over the mean key of blocks of 4 tokens, in Qwen's QSA.

neuronio-morto.d: A ReLU neuron whose pre-activation became negative for every input: its output and its gradient are zero forever, and it stops learning.

softplus.d: \( \ln(1+e^{z}) \), a smooth, always-positive ReLU with derivative \( \sigma(z) \). Used in the decay of Qwen's Gated DeltaNet and in the sqrtsoftplus score of DeepSeek's router.

gelu.d: \( z\,\Phi(z) \), with \( \Phi \) the cumulative distribution of the standard normal. It has an approximate variant, gelu_pytorch_tanh, declared in Qwen's ViT; DeepSeek's Aligner uses the exact one (F.gelu). The two differ by up to ~5×10⁻⁴.

silu.d: \( z\,\sigma(z) \): the input multiplied by its own sigmoid. Smooth and non-monotonic (minimum ≈ −0.278). It is the hidden_act of the three recipe LLMs, as the gate branch of SwiGLU, and it appears in the short convolutions of KDA and GDN.

mlp.d: A network of linear layers interleaved with activations, for example \( W_2 f(W_1\mathbf x+\mathbf b_1)+\mathbf b_2 \). The FFN of each Transformer block is an MLP (a gated one, in SwiGLU form).

aproximacao-universal.d: Theorem (Cybenko 1989; Hornik 1991; Leshno et al. 1993): an MLP with one hidden layer and a non-polynomial activation approximates any continuous function on a bounded domain, given enough neurons. It guarantees existence, not efficiency or ease of training.

gating.d: Multiplying a signal, elementwise, by an opening computed from the data itself, typically \( \sigma(W_g\mathbf x) \in (0,1) \). It decides how much passes, bounds magnitudes and creates multiplicative interactions. It is a central theme of Qwen3.8's architecture.

glu.d: \( \sigma(W_g\mathbf x)\odot W_u\mathbf x \) (Dauphin et al., 2017). Swapping the sigmoid for GELU or SiLU gives GeGLU and SwiGLU (Shazeer, 2020), the FFNs of modern LLMs.

grafo-computacional.d: A representation of a computation as a graph of simple operations. In the forward pass, values flow from the inputs to the loss; in the backward pass, gradients flow from the loss to the parameters.

regra-da-cadeia.d: The derivative of a composition is the product of the local derivatives: \( \partial L/\partial w = (\partial L/\partial a)(\partial a/\partial z)(\partial z/\partial w) \). When there are several paths, their contributions add up.

jacobiano.d: The matrix of all partial derivatives of a vector function, \( J_{ij} = \partial y_i/\partial x_j \). In backprop, the gradient crosses a layer multiplied by the transpose of its Jacobian.

backpropagation.d: The algorithm that computes the gradient of the loss with respect to every parameter in a single backward pass through the graph, applying the chain rule layer by layer: \( \boldsymbol\delta = f'(\mathbf z)\odot W_{\text{next}}^\top\boldsymbol\delta_{\text{next}} \).

diferenciacao-automatica.d: A technique that obtains exact derivatives of a program by composing the derivatives of its elementary operations. Reverse mode (backprop) gives the gradient of every parameter at a cost on the order of two forward passes. At inference it is turned off.

diferenca-finita.d: A numerical approximation of the derivative, \( [L(w+h)-L(w-h)]/(2h) \). Useful for checking a gradient, but it requires extra passes for each parameter: infeasible for billions of them.

largura.d: The number of neurons in a layer. In an LLM, the hidden_size (4096 in GLM and DeepSeek, 2560 in Qwen) and the intermediate widths of the FFNs and experts.

profundidade.d: The number of layers in sequence (45 in GLM, 48 in Qwen, 43 in DeepSeek). It increases compositional power, but it is sequential: it goes straight into each token's latency.

layernorm.d: Per-token normalization: \( \boldsymbol\gamma\odot(\mathbf x-\mu)/\sqrt{\sigma^2+\varepsilon}+\boldsymbol\beta \). It centers, rescales and has a bias. It appears in Qwen's ViT and in the k_norm of GLM's indexer.

rmsnorm.d: Per-token normalization without centering: \( \boldsymbol\gamma\odot\mathbf x/\sqrt{\operatorname{mean}(x_i^2)+\varepsilon} \). It brings the vector to RMS ≈ 1 (norm ≈ \( \sqrt d \)) and applies a learned per-coordinate gain. Cheaper than LayerNorm (it doesn't subtract the mean) and used in the decoders of the three models: before the sublayers, in MLA latents and on queries and keys (QK-Norm). ε (rms_norm_eps): 1e-5 in GLM, 1e-6 in Qwen, 1e-20/1e-6 in DeepSeek.

epsilon-da-norma.d: A small number added to the mean of squares (or to the variance) before the square root, to avoid dividing by zero. It dominates when the input's RMS is smaller than \( \sqrt\varepsilon \). Values: GLM 1e-5 (vision forced to 1e-6), Qwen 1e-6, DeepSeek Vision-Exp 1e-20 in the text trunk (the ViT uses 1e-6; 0731 uses 1e-6).

invariancia-de-escala.d: A property of RMSNorm (and LayerNorm): multiplying the input by \( \alpha>0 \) doesn't change the output, as long as ε is negligible. It keeps the scale of one layer from contaminating the next.

ganho-zero-centrado.d: A convention in which the norm's weight is stored as a deviation from 1: initialized at 0 and applied as \( 1+w \). Used in Qwen3.8's RMSNorms; DeepSeek stores the gain directly, initialized at 1. Mixing up the two breaks the model.

gradiente-evanescente.d: What happens when the gradient crosses many layers and is repeatedly multiplied by factors smaller than 1: it shrinks exponentially and the first layers stop learning.

gradiente-explosivo.d: The opposite of the vanishing gradient: per-layer factors greater than 1 make the gradient grow exponentially with depth and destabilize training.

conexao-residual.d: \( \mathbf h_{\ell+1} = \mathbf h_\ell + F_\ell(\mathbf h_\ell) \): each layer adds a correction instead of replacing the vector. The Jacobian gains an identity term, and the gradient reaches the first layers without vanishing (He et al., 2015).
